svg.aria-label: Diagram: the three Microsoft Entra writeback features compared. Password writeback is synchronous and real time over an Azure Service Bus relay, outbound only on port 443, with the password encrypted using a 2048-bit RSA key inside a package encrypted with AES-GCM at a key size of 256 bits, keys rolling over every six months, a heartbeat message once every five minutes, and messages typically under 1 KB; it enforces the on-premises Active Directory password policy through the SetPassword API, which means the on-premises policy wins even when it is weaker than the cloud policy, and it cannot reset passwords for members of protected groups. Device writeback takes up to 3 hours, requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or P2, requires the forest schema at Windows 2012 R2 level, permits only one device registration configuration object per forest, requires devices to be in the same forest as users so multiple user forests are unsupported, and exists for Windows Hello for Business hybrid certificate trust and for Conditional Access to AD FS protected applications. Group writeback v2 in Connect Sync is deprecated and no longer supported, with Cloud Sync provisioning cloud security groups instead on a job that runs every 20 minutes, needing the msDS-ExternalDirectoryObjectId attribute from Windows Server 2016, provisioning agent 1.1.2334.0, Connect Sync 2.2.8.0, and domain controller access on TCP/389 and TCP/3268; its scale limits are 10K groups and 250K membership links in Selected security groups mode, 20K groups and 500K links in All security groups mode with an attribute filter, no group larger than 50K members, and the portal pane lists only 999 groups. A closing panel notes that members without an AD DS account are silently skipped and that Microsoft 365 groups stay on Group Writeback v1.
svg.title: One arrow reversed, three times, by three mechanisms that share nothing but a name
svg.text: Sync runs one way. Three features run the other way, and they are in three different states of health.
Once the cloud can write into Active Directory, the directory is no longer the sole authority over its own contents.
Three writebacks, three transports, three latencies
FEATURE
TRANSPORT AND LATENCY
STATE OF HEALTH
Password writeback
Service Bus relay, outbound 443 only
synchronous — “zero-delay feedback”
mature; the one most tenants run
Device writeback
Connect Sync only
“up to 3 hours” to appear in AD
narrow: AD FS relying parties, and
certificate-trust Windows Hello. Nothing else.
Group writeback
Cloud Sync job, every 20 minutes
v2 on Connect Sync is “deprecated and no
longer supported” — migrate to Cloud Sync
The weaker policy wins, and that is correct
“There’s a chance that the on-premises password policy is
weaker than the cloud password policy. In this case,
the on-premises policy is enforced.”
The agent calls the AD DS SetPassword API, so AD itself
judges history, complexity, age and password filters.
There is no way around it that keeps the feature working:
a password the cloud accepts and AD rejects would work
in Microsoft 365 and fail at the domain-joined laptop.
On the wire, and what it costs to run
Password encrypted with a 2048-bit RSA key; the whole
package then with AES-GCM at a key size of 256 bits.
Keys roll over every six months. The relay carries “a
randomly generated strong password that Microsoft
never has access to.”
Heartbeat once every five minutes, two messages per
reset, each “typically under 1 KB”. No inbound rules.
A request left waiting “times out and is removed”.
The exclusions that break a helpdesk runbook
Reset from the Entra admin center
written back
Reset from the Microsoft 365 admin center
not written back — same action, different portal
PowerShell v1 or v2, or Graph self-reset
not written back
A member of a protected group
the service account cannot reset it — see post #47
User has “Password never expires” set
the force-change flag is never written, and nothing says so
Staged rollout enabled for the group
unsupported, during the migration Microsoft recommends
Group writeback is governed by hard numbers, not guidance
SCOPING MODE
GROUPS
DIRECT MEMBERSHIP LINKS
Selected security groups
up to 10K
up to 250K across all groups in scope
All security groups, with an attribute filter
up to 20K
up to 500K across all groups in scope
All security groups, no filter
“not supported”
Plus a ceiling independent of mode: no group over 50K members. The portal pane lists only 999 groups, so scoping past a
thousand becomes a Graph appRoleAssignedTo call per group — beyond that point, scoping is code rather than configuration.
And the pattern once more: “a cloud-managed user that has no AD DS account is skipped.” A written-back group that gates
an application grants access to fewer people than it lists, with no error. Count the members on both sides.
Sources: On-premises password writeback with SSPR, Microsoft Entra Connect: Enabling device writeback, and Group writeback with Cloud Sync, on Microsoft Learn.
